4th November 2289, 0533 hours

Laurius

They had been far too late to save the world, it was the first to fall to the Golden Fleet and her refugees had been massacred in orbit. Nearly eight and a half billion souls were lost during the fight, probably an even billion scattered in the ring of junk that would spend millennia kissing the atmosphere. When they went in he wondered why they would be going to a dead world, what possible motive the brass had for sending their best killers to a world they already lost. Surely a snatch and grab of some bullshit junk would be better suited for the fucking rangers, but he had his orders.

Even from orbit he could see the world was a lost cause, they had a pair of Laurius natives and the look on their faces must have been the same he wore when they revisited Neuwa. They looked like hate made a pair of people, and the metallic taste flooded his own memory; on his first op he had clenched his teeth so hard his gums bled.

"Chief, the fuck is that?"

Stan leaned around the bulkhead and looked over the pilot's shoulder. "A whole goddamn freighter, some hotshot set her down right in the river."

Neuwans were experts at that, taking something huge in orbit and riding it down for easier access. Maybe they had some salty hulk surfer on board?

"I'm setting you down right here, we're on passive right now but something down there painted us for a second."

That seemed reasonable enough. "Whatever you say, Lieutenant. I reckon we'll be good anyway."

Once on the ground he didn't linger and neither did the dropship, once the team was off it was gone to go hide somewhere else. Fortunately nobody was around to care besides the murderous robots left behind, but they weren't fast enough to converge on the LZ. Behind him Corporal Ayla Younan was already forming up, he liked that about her a lot. There was a specialist from the army, Chiug Dathswa, a teganti electronics and explosives expert who was new to the unit who lingered near a building a little bit too long for Stan's liking.

"Cheggy, the fuck you doing?" he thought, the display on his helmet put the sentence into text characters.

Instead of using a radio the message was a much, much more clandestine method and incredibly difficult to detect. Unfortunately somebody needed to have a CBI installed, the clunky module replaced a portion of his skull and the small data port behind his ear had a habit of itching like a motherfucker. When it came down to it though he liked not being shot at more than being comfortable, so the trade-off was well worth it.

Soon a reply typed across his vision. "Found some bodies."

He looked down and scowled at the half-rotten face at his feet, there were bodies everywhere. "Suck it the fuck up, soldier."

"It's a family."

Oh.

That changed the circumstances a bit, the numbers from Tegantu were still coming in and nobody knew who made it out or who didn't. Somewhere, hopefully, was the three children Cheggy had fathered along with his bubbly, lovable wife in some refugee center. Those weren't always safe either, it was becoming clear that the situation for civilians was getting really dangerous and Seylonis itself might need to become the primary collection point. Shitty deal.

"Okay, Cheggy, we came here to do a job. Don't flake out on me."

Another message came across the net, this time from their fourth member Sergeant Nick Hauser. "Movement to our seven. Two walkers inbound."

Alarm shot through Stan like a goddamn lightning bolt, but he didn't even need to give the order. Cheggy and Hauser set up behind a ruined bus, while Younan got her distance and set up at the top of some apartment building's staircase. When the walkers marched to the location the four were ready, but communication ceased; walkers honed in on transmissions easily.

Popping up from the concrete barricade he hid behind, Stan took quick aim and fired off a grenade square into the side of the first walker.

That attracted their attention, and he dropped down before they could respond. Each walker was armed with three sets of three gun barrels, they rotated around a complex planetary gearbox that fed from three magazines inside the four-legged monstrosity's hull. Each cluster of barrels would fire and feed independently, but it was the combined force of all three that made them absurdly deadly to nearly anything. When they opened up they could eat through most barricades with sustained fire, a technique called jackhammering, and with armor-piercing shells they could give tanks cause for concern.

Worse still was the sound of it all. He slinked down and bolted along the river bank toward Ayla's position, but the high pitched whine, almost like an otherworldly moan, of the rapid-firing gun barrels stole his breath and filled him with irrational terror; every hair on his body stood up at that sound.

Stan snapped awake in a cold sweat.

His heart apparently didn't get the memo because he had to gasp for air to keep up with it, adrenaline surged through his veins as the sickly sensation of his terror slinking back into it's cage made his skin crawl. Every fiber of his being wanted to spring out of himself, just to get the fuck away from all of that shit. His mind whispered memories of alcohol taking him away, giving him relief, he thirsted for a drink but held fast. Substance abuse would make him sloppy, he needed to be sharp. Strong.

A killer.

There were still dangers outside his happy little life, he was a father again and soon he would be married. Concentration on the web of arms, legs, and tails around him helped the feelings slide away and he inhaled deeply to clear it out. His nose took in the musky odor of the tawaunan next to him, and the hot warmth of both his lovers radiated into the realm of his perception. That was enough for him to build some good feelings, to manufacture a sensation of safety.

He closed his eyes and dared to sleep again.

12th May 2556, 1018 hours

Kriegsmark, Galley

Stan slowly stirred the mix of vegetables and meats on the pan, the warm aroma of a home-cooked meal wafting through the air. Behind him the children were playing quietly as they waited for him to finish cooking breakfast, and to his left Jade sat on the couch at the far end of the room as she watched the view screen across the galley. Lips pressed to the back of his neck which made him freeze momentarily, a familiar tongue lashing out to toy with his ear.

"Sleep well?" he asked as Inzili slipped her arms around his midsection. "That ear thing is way less sexy when I'm busy."

Of course she had to do it again, making sure the tip slobbered around over the hole until he twisted his head away. Too bad for him, she didn't even have to move to reach his new position with her lengthy tongue.

"You can fuckin' stop that any time now."

She giggled and kissed him. "Yes, I sleep well. Did you?"

"Just like I do most other nights," he lied, but he continued something sincere, "helps to be the meat in the sandwich."

Before he could react Jade sauntered past and snatched up a chunk of meat, scarfing it down. "Tasty."

"That was raw, babe. Gross."

All that did was give her a slight pause as she looked up in thought before she shrugged and kept walking. Truly she was a bottomless pit, somehow she had the intestinal fortitude to handle such a voracious appetite too.

"Somebody is in good mood," Inzili murmured, kissing his neck to show her loyalty.

After pondering a few minutes about teasing him, she released ran her hands up inside his shirt, her fingers tracing along the line of fur that extended down from his chest. None of it was real fur, that would have been gross, but somehow a human with a hairy chest was... fun. Especially him, and she buried her nose into his neck before inhaling sharply. That was something he had gotten used to, so he only had to resist a mild urge to shudder from the pins and needles running up his spine. Humans were ticklish basically everywhere, sometimes she forgot that!

"Gonna need your pipes today."

"Mmm? Jade can't help?"

"She's got other jobs. Sure is nice to have her around, I hate doin' computer stuff by myself."

She didn't know anything about computers, so she shrugged and changed the subject. "I like my male make food for our family, you are very well-trained."

That was obvious teasing but she was quite sincere in that she loved Stan doing the "man things" like cooking, cleaning, and other mundane chores that she had always felt were men's work. Even though she knew her sense of "gender roles" was either skewed or just contrary to what everyone else had, it still made her feel good to have him live up to that "dream mate" persona she had made when she was young. Though he seemed to enjoy the byplay more than she would have expected when they first met and she enjoyed it too; life was fun when he pushed back.

Stirring as he chuckled, Stan turned slightly. "On one hand I know that's a compliment and on the other I know you're givin' me shit... either way yes, I love you too, good morning, now... mind gettin' the girls ready?"

Inzili didn't reply in words, instead he just felt her lips press to his cheek before she released him to resume his work. Stan knew the dish was a hit with the whole family, a mix of wild vegetables, herbs, mushrooms, and smoked local meat that the locals had traded to him. Preparation was easy too, just dice everything up tiny, throw it in a pan, and then fry it until the potato-looking things turned brown. Both girls were still breastfeeding but they were easily old enough to eat solid food, Akisa just had a bit more trouble with it due to having far less teeth than her sister.

"Do you two love your daddy's cooking?" she asked softly, running the back of her fingers down their backs. "I think we are lucky to have man who knows how to cook."
